question: The ‘Tripartite struggle’ was between Gurjara Pratiharas in North India, Palas in Eastern India and ________ in South India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rashtrakutas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tripartite Struggle**, also known as the** Kannauj Triangle Wars,** unfolded in the 9th century as a fierce conflict between three powerful empires: the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire, the Pala Empire, and the Rashtrakuta Empire.
 
• These empires vied for control over the Gangetic region in northern India, with the pivotal battleground being the fertile area of Kannauj.
 
• The Rashtrakutas, initially feudatories of the Chalukyas, established their dominance and had their capital at Manyakheta or Malkhed near Sholapur.
 
• They emerged victorious in the Tripartite Struggle, defeating both the Palas and the Pratiharas, thereby consolidating their influence over the region.
 
• This conflict marked a significant chapter in Indian history, shaping the political landscape of northern India during the medieval period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Rashtrakutas **were a prominent Indian dynasty that held sway over extensive territories across the Indian subcontinent from the 6th to the 10th centuries CE.
 
• The earliest known Rashtrakuta inscription dates back to the 7th century, recorded on a copper plate grant that delineates their authority from Manapur, a city located in Central or West India.
 
• Additional inscriptions from the same era mention other Rashtrakuta rulers, including those of Achalapur and Kannauj.
 
• Despite their historical significance, controversies persist regarding the origins of the early Rashtrakutas, their native homeland, and even their language.
 
• Scholars continue to explore various theories and hypotheses to shed light on these aspects of Rashtrakuta history, contributing to ongoing debates within the field of Indian history and archaeology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Maratha Empire** was a significant Indian power in the early modern era and later evolved into a confederation that governed large swathes of the Indian subcontinent during the 18th century.
 
• **The Cholas** are remembered as one of the longest-reigning dynasties in southern India.
 
• **The Chera dynasty, **a Hindu dynasty from the Sangam age, unified various regions along the western coast and western ghats of southern India to establish the early Chera empire.
